# Hermes proof harness

Scripts written for the 2026-10-04 pass, to prove on real hardware what the test suite covers in
simulation. They are test scaffolding, not product code: nothing in `packages/`, `music-player/`,
`docker-container/`, `windows-companion/` or `android/` imports them.

Every machine path comes from the environment — `NP_SCRATCH` (a disposable folder) and `NP_CLONE`
(the clone) — so nothing here carries a path from the machine it was written on.

**No credential is committed.** The hub password is generated by `hub-api.mjs setup`, written to
`$NP_SCRATCH/hub-secrets.json`, and read back at run time. Pairing codes and fingerprints are
printed to the console for the operator to use and are never written to a committed file.

| Script | What it is for | Which section |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hub-api.mjs` | Drives a hub over its own HTTP API: first-run setup, provider health, download jobs. | §2.2, §2.3 |
| `start-companion.mjs` | Launches the **packaged** companion with `PORTABLE_EXECUTABLE_DIR`/`NP_DATA_DIR` pointed at the scratch folder, optionally with every ffmpeg directory removed from `PATH`. | §2.4 |
| `companion-ui.mjs` | Drives the packaged companion through Playwright-Electron: dumps every control, screenshots a named section. | §2.4, §2.12 |
| `live-tv-setup.mjs` | Adds an M3U playlist and an XMLTV guide through the companion's own Live TV tab. | §2.5 |
| `pair-all.mjs` | Pairs companion and hub in one browser session (the hub's pending session belongs to the signed-in operator, so it cannot span two). | §2.5 |
| `uia-folder-picker.ps1` | Drives Windows' native folder picker through UI Automation, by `ValuePattern` and `InvokePattern` rather than keystrokes. | §2.5 |
| `uia-foreground.ps1` / `uia-invoke.ps1` / `uia-dump.ps1` | Identify a window by exact title **and** owning PID, assert it is foreground, then act. | §0 |
| `android-webview.mjs` | Talks CDP straight to the Android WebView's page target (Playwright's `connectOverCDP` cannot drive a WebView). | §2.6 |
| `android-drive.sh` | `adb input`-only driving of the installed APK, for screenshots. | §2.6 |
| `talk-headline.mjs` | Tunes a named station by its own `data-sid` row and reads the player's headline. | §2.7 |
| `helper-lan.mjs` | Drives Settings ▸ Network's LAN toggle and probes the four read routes over this PC's own LAN address. | §2.9 |
| `companion-downloads.mjs` | Sets the Downloads options and runs two real fetches through the helper's own API. | §2.11 |
| `controls-companion.mjs` | One pass over the companion's new controls, clicked by DOM position. | §2.12 |
| `controls-hub.mjs` | One pass over the hub's new controls: backup schedule, Network Save/Revert, scan, Discord wording. | §2.12 |
| `export-logs.mjs` | Runs the shipped bundle's own `redactLog` over the real log and the real helper token. | §2.12 |
| `folder-picker.mjs` | Clicks **Add Folder…** with a *trusted* click, then drives the native dialog through UI Automation — path by `ValuePattern`, button by `InvokePattern`, no keystrokes. | §2.5 |
| `metered-check.ps1` | Reports the connection cost through the companion's own `COST_SCRIPT`, so "is this PC metered" is answered by the same call the product makes. | §2.10 |
| `metered-decision.mjs` | Runs the shipped bundle's own `classifyCost()` and `streamingDecision()` against the exact lines Windows produced. | §2.10 |
| `metered-live.mjs` | Drives Remote ▸ streaming with a real metered connection and reads the supervisor's own `running` / `blocked` state either side of the switch. | §2.10 |

## Things that cost time, so they are written down

Each of these was a harness fault that first read as a product fault. They are the reason several
"FAIL" lines in this pass's transcripts turned out to be wrong:

- **A radio station is tuned with a single click**, not a double-click. `music-player/index.html`
  binds `click` to `radioChoose`; a dblclick also fires the `pointerdown`/`pointerup` pair the same
  view treats as a click-drag, and the drag cancels the tune.
- **Playwright's `connectOverCDP` cannot drive a WebView** — it speaks the browser-level protocol and a
  WebView has no browser-level context management. `android-webview.mjs` connects to the page target's
  WebSocket and speaks CDP directly.
- **The hub's pending pairing session belongs to one signed-in operator.** Minting a code in one
  browser and confirming it in another signs in again, and the session is gone. That is the hub
  behaving correctly; `pair-all.mjs` does both halves in one run.
- **The companion's Downloaders buttons read only "Check" / "Update"**, with the tool named in a
  sibling element, inside a 2,499px scroller in a 760px window. Name matching finds three identical
  buttons and off-screen clicks time out, so `controls-companion.mjs` targets by position in the
  section.
- **`Revert` is `disabled={!dirty}`.** Clicking it with nothing unsaved is not a defect; it is
  correctly disabled. It puts back what the *hub* has, for edits not yet saved.
- **The native dialogs need a trusted click to open at all.** A synthetic `element.click()` from
  `page.evaluate` did not open the folder picker and closed the companion.
- **A dialog opened with `showOpenDialog(parentWindow, …)` is an OWNED window**, so it is a
  *descendant* of the app's top-level window, not a sibling under the desktop root. Searching
  only the root's children reports "no window titled …" **while the dialog is plainly on
  screen** — which is what `uia-folder-picker.ps1` did, twice, before it was made to print what
  *was* on screen on failure. Look for the shell dialog class (`#32770`) under
  `TreeScope::Descendants`.
- **The dialog is not owned by the pid a launcher hands back.** It was pid 67376 when Playwright
  launched pid 76056, because Electron hosts it in whichever process of the app's tree owns it.
  Require the owning *executable* (`-ExpectedProcessName`), not one pid.
  With all three fixed, `folder-picker.mjs` chooses a folder with no person involved.
- **Export Logs is the exception.** `showSaveDialog` blocks the main thread the same way, but its
  dialog is not needed to answer the question the brief asks, so `export-logs.mjs` runs the
  shipped bundle's own `redactLog` instead.
- **Clear Cache** emptied nothing measurable in this sandbox because the other cache slices were
  already empty; the button ran without error. That is not evidence that it clears a full cache.
- **Grant `library:share` before testing §2.5's sharing claim.** `library:share` is deliberately not
  in the hub's `DEFAULT_SCOPES` (`docker-container/src/web/views/Devices.tsx:20`), so pairing without
  ticking "Share from the library" produces a companion that correctly refuses to share. Reading that
  as "sharing does not start by itself" is how the first version of this report claimed a defect that
  does not exist. `pair-all.mjs --grant-share` does the tick. A security default read as a bug is the
  most expensive kind of harness fault, because the report then asks Claude Code to "fix" the
  protection.
- **Read the hub's Live TV from its API, not from the Music tab's heading.** "Live TV from the
  companion" is static explanatory copy in `docker-container/src/web/views/LiveTv.tsx:21`, shown
  whether or not there is data behind it, so grepping the page for that string proves nothing in
  either direction. `live-tv-to-hub.mjs` reads `GET /api/v1/live-tv` as the signed-in admin.
- **The "Hub connection" fieldset only renders while unpaired.** A credential left over from an
  earlier run means `getByLabel('Hub address')` never appears, which looks like the Remote tab failing
  to load. `pair-all.mjs` forgets the stored hub first — which is also §2.5's own "a second hub
  refuses the old credential" step, done deliberately.

- **Windows reports the cost of the connection in use, and on one LAN that is not the one you marked.**
  With Wi-Fi and Ethernet on the same subnet, `GetInternetConnectionProfile()` returns the wired
  profile and `WifiAdapterId` is empty — and raising the Wi-Fi interface metric changes the routing
  without changing that. The metered profile only becomes the internet profile when the wired adapter
  leaves the connection. Read `.agents/evidence/harness/metered-check.ps1` before concluding a metered setting "did not
  take".
- **`Set-NetIPInterface` needs an Administrator shell.** An unelevated one returns
  `Access is denied`, so interface-metric changes are the owner's to make and undo.
- **The companion is single-instance** (`main/security.ts:141`), so a second launch forwards to the
  running one and exits instead of opening a window — which looks exactly like a launch failure.
- **The AWSP status object carries a huge `ticketQrSvg`.** Print only the fields under test; dumping
  the whole object buries the result in an SVG path.
